extracted.intended_audience: U.S. institutions of higher education (university investigators and research administrators) preparing white papers and full proposals for the Department of Defense FY2025 MURI program
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit white papers and full grant proposals in response to the DoD FY2025 MURI Funding Opportunity Announcement, following program-specific eligibility, format, content, and submission rules and responding to topic-specific concentration areas and resource limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper deadline / timing
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers must be received no later than 17 May 2024 at 5:00 PM Eastern Time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: White papers are OPTIONAL but strongly recommended; Questions regarding white papers have an earlier inquiry deadline (03 May 2024). White papers submitted after the deadline may not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: White papers encouraged (purpose of white paper)
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers are OPTIONAL but strongly recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: White papers minimize labor and cost for applicants and allow the Research Topic Chief to provide informal feedback (encourage/discourage submission or suggest re-teaming) based on assessment of the white paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper format constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper size 8.5 x 11-inch; 1-inch margins; single-spaced; Times New Roman, 12-point; page limit no more than four (4) single-sided pages (excluding cover letter, cover page, and curriculum vitae).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: White paper pages beyond the 4-page limit may not be evaluated or read.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper required content elements
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers shall include a cover sheet (FOA number, proposed title, proposer's technical POC with telephone, fax, email, topic number and title) and provide proposed technical approaches; potential impact on DoD capabilities; potential team and management plan; summary of estimated costs; curriculum vitae of key investigators; identification of any Organizational Conflict(s) of Interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ONR submissions use the specific cover sheet downloadable from ONR; white papers should provide sufficient technical information (hypothesis, theories, approaches, data measurements/analysis) to allow assessment by a technical expert; white papers need not carry institutional signatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper submission methods and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission pathways vary by agency: ONR white papers via FedConnect; ARO via e-mail/USPS/commercial carrier to the Research Topic Chief; AFOSR via APAN submission page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT use the FedConnect message center to submit white papers or questions; hard copy white papers should be stapled in the upper left-hand corner (no plastic covers or binders); separate attachments (brochures, reprints) will not be accepted; do NOT email ZIP or password-protected files.

rubrics_metrics.name: FedConnect and SAM registration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants applying online through FedConnect must register with the System for Award Management (SAM) and receive a unique entity identifier (UEI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAM registration must be renewed annually; first person to register in FedConnect will need the SAM MPIN; then create a FedConnect account. FedConnect how-to guide and support contact information provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal submission and Grants.gov validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be ‘VALIDATED’ by Grants.gov by the application deadline, which can take up to 48 hours after successful submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is strongly recommended that applications be submitted at least 2 business days ahead of the stated deadline to allow time for validation and any necessary resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal technical proposal formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical Proposal: paper size 8.5 x 11 inch; 1-inch margins; single-spaced; Times New Roman, 12-point; page limit — Technical Proposal: 25 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no page limitations for the budget. The technical proposal/page count includes the Technical Approach/Project Narrative; items listed as NOT included in page count (if specified elsewhere) are excluded. Follow exact page-count rules in Section II.D.2.c.

rubrics_metrics.name: File attachment requirements (full proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Files attached to forms must be in Adobe PDF; cannot contain macros; and cannot be password protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any attachment is not a PDF, contains macros or is password protected it will not pass the automated acceptance check and will need to be resubmitted prior to the submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic file name length restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The electronic file name for all documents submitted under this FOA must not exceed 68 characters in length, including the file name extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to adhere to file name length may trigger submission problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF-424 special field completion instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete all required SF-424 (R&R) fields; special instructions include field-specific entries: Field 4a (For ONR enter 'N00014'; For ARO 'W36QYT'; For AFOSR 'FA9550'), Field 4b (Agency Routing Number: ONR enter 3-digit Research Topic Chief’s Code and name in brackets; ARO enter Research Topic Chief name; AFOSR enter Topic Number and name in brackets), Field 11 include 'MURI:' at beginning of title and include ONR White Paper Tracking Number, Field 7 select 'Other' for Minority-Serving Institution and note it as MI where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete SF-424 first because it auto-populates some fields on other forms. Applicants who fail to provide a Program Officer Code identifier may receive notice that their proposal is rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project abstract public release requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A project abstract is required with the application and must be publicly releasable as specified in Section II.D.2.c.(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare an abstract suitable for public release and follow the precise instructions in the referenced section to avoid disclosure issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary information marking and legend
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposals containing data the Applicant does not want disclosed, the Applicant shall mark the title page with a specific legend and mark each sheet of data that the Applicant wishes to restrict with the indicated sheet legend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact legend language provided in the FOA on the title page and on each restricted sheet; the restriction applies only for evaluation/program coordination and does not prevent the Government's right to use information obtained from other sources without restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator participation across multiple proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants contemplating use of an individual as PI for more than one proposal/topic are strongly encouraged to contact the Topic Chief(s) prior to white paper submission to determine Topic Chief support for PI participation in multiple proposals and/or topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI participation in multiple proposals must be identified in white papers and proposals; document percent effort/availability and how PI will manage time if multiple awards occur. Topic Chief support is discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of current and pending research (conflict of commitment/coi)
rubrics_metrics.description: This announcement requires disclosure of all current and pending research support as defined by Section 223 of the FY21 National Defense Authorization Act for all covered individuals (key personnel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure must be complete at time of proposal and updated annually during performance; failure to report fully may be considered a material statement under the False Claims Act. The funding agency may conduct pre-award COI/conflict-of-commitment reviews (NSPM-33); significant conflicts may be basis for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of applicants (who may apply / receive MURI funds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition open only to U.S. institutions of higher education (universities) with degree-granting programs in science and/or engineering, including DoD institutions of higher education; UARCs are eligible to submit/receive MURI funds only to the extent they are part of a U.S. institution and not designated as FFRDCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ineligible organizations (industry, DoD labs, FFRDCs, foreign entities) may collaborate but may not receive MURI funds directly or via subaward. When additional funding for an ineligible organization is necessary, a separate supplemental proposal from that organization may be attached and evaluated by the Topic Chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost sharing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost sharing is not expected and will not be used as a factor during the merit review of any application under this FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Government may consider voluntary cost sharing if proposed, but it is not required nor scored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracted fundamental research definition & responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracted fundamental research includes research performed under grants/contracts that are (a) funded by RDT&E Budget Activity 1 (Basic Research) or (b) funded by Budget Activity 2 (Applied Research) and performed on campus at a university. Research funded by other activities or performed off-campus may not meet the definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential Applicants should consult DoD Technical POCs to determine whether effort constitutes fundamental or non-fundamental research. If subcontractors perform fundamental research while prime does not, prime must identify and describe the subcontracted research and include a statement confirming scoping and determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument type and ARO cooperative agreement vs grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards will take the form of grants; for ARO, awards may be grants and/or cooperative agreements. Cooperative agreements imply substantial involvement by the Federal Government; grants imply no substantial involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee or profit allowed on grants/cooperative agreements. Prospective Applicants should contact the technical POC to understand DoD expected substantial involvement for cooperative agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funded amount and period of performance expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Total amount available for the five years for grants resulting from this FOA estimated at approximately $200M pending appropriations; typical annual funding per grant is up to $1.5M; award size and number of supported researchers generally should not exceed topic-specified limits listed in Section II.H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards contingent on availability of funds and scope of proposed work. Applicants are strongly recommended to discuss funding and team size with Research Topic Chiefs before submitting formal proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: HBCU/MI additional funding eligibility and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For select topics (4, 6, 10, 15, 17, and 21) an additional $1.5M per topic over the 5-year MURI award is available specifically to support HBCU/MI participation in the MURI team; HBCU/MI team members are not required for submission to these topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be considered for the additional funding, the HBCU/MI participant must satisfy eligibility in 10 U.S.C. § 4144 (covered educational institutions). Eligible applicants should provide the Department of Education letter dated in the year of application certifying eligibility under Title III or Title V; for non-HBCU/TCU MSIs, failure to include this letter with the full proposal WILL result in not being considered for the additional funding. Additional funding must be allocated to HBCU/MI team members and must be fully integrated into the MURI team with a single technical narrative and cost application.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper technical detail requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers should provide sufficient information on the research (e.g., hypothesis, theories, concepts, approaches, data measurements and analysis) to allow for an assessment by a technical expert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: White papers are not required to carry official institutional signatures. Level of detail should allow the Topic Chief to assess and provide meaningful feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required forms and acceptable formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective Applicants must complete the mandatory SF-424 Research and Related (R&R) family forms and any other mandatory forms found at Grants.gov; attachments must conform to PDF/macro/password rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete SF-424 first; follow pop-up instructions and FOA-specific exceptions (special instructions for particular fields). Non-conforming files will fail automated checks and require resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard copy handling and unacceptable attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Hard copy white papers should be stapled in the upper left-hand corner; plastic covers or binders should not be used. Separate attachments such as individual brochures or reprints will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow agency-specific submission instructions. Do NOT submit attachments in ZIP or password-protected forms or use FedConnect message center for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Conflict(s) of Interest identification
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers and proposals must identify any Organizational Conflict(s) of Interest (if any) as described in Section II.F.2.m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include conflict identification in white paper and full proposal; follow Section II.F.2.m for detail on required disclosures and handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of proposals (confidentiality and return policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The DoD agencies treat all white papers and proposals submitted under this FOA as sensitive competitive information and will disclose contents only for purposes of evaluation. Technical and budget proposals (or any other material) submitted in response to this FOA will not be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should mark proprietary information appropriately; understand that proposals are protected from unauthorized disclosure in accordance with law and DoD regulations but will not be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external subject-matter-expert advisors in evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisors external to the U.S. government may be used as subject-matter-expert technical consultants in the evaluation of proposals after signing non-disclosure statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is noted to inform applicants that outside experts may review proposal content under NDA; no further action required by applicants beyond marking proprietary data as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and updates monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should be alert for any amendments that may modify the announcement; amendments will be posted to Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodically check the listed websites (Grants.gov, ONR, AFOSR, ARO) for updates and amendments prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-specific anticipated resources & team size limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Topic Description (Section II.H) lists anticipated resources (typical $1.5M/year for 5 years) and a recommended maximum number of funded faculty researchers (commonly 6–8 depending on topic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers should generally not exceed the limit specified for the individual topics; exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with topic chiefs during the white paper phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals for supplementation of existing projects not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for supplementation of existing projects will not be accepted under this FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit new, independent proposals that do not request supplement funds to ongoing projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely receipt proof & Grants.gov validation special note
rubrics_metrics.description: SPECIAL NOTE: Applications must be ‘VALIDATED’ by Grants.gov by the application deadline, which can take up to 48 hours after successful submission. See Section II.D.6.d.i. Timely Receipt Requirements and Proof of Timely Submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for validation time and keep proof of timely submission; recommended to submit at least 2 business days ahead of deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal title guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles given to submissions should be descriptive of the work they cover and not be merely a copy of the title of this announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For SF-424 Field 11 include 'MURI:' at the beginning of your descriptive title and include the ONR White Paper Tracking Number (for ONR submissions).
